svg.text: Scalable Web Application with ALB and Auto Scaling (EC2-Based)
Manara Tech · AWS Solutions Architect Associate graduation project · Region: us-east-1 (N. Virginia)
SG-EC2: app port from SG-ALB only
SG-EC2: app port from SG-ALB only
EC2 Auto Scaling Group (one ASG spanning AZ A and AZ B)
nodes in Public Subnet A + Public Subnet B
AWS WAF Web ACL (OWASP Top 10 rules)
associated with this ALB: inspects and filters requests
sync replica, not an app server
Route 53 Alias points to the ALB.
ASG configuration (same ASG, AZ A + B)
Session Manager ↔ SSM Agent (no bastion, no SSH)
EC2 requires an IAM Instance Profile and
through NAT Gateway or VPC Endpoints.
Icon tiles use AWS category colours; replace with the official AWS Architecture Icons if required.
1 Users query Route 53 for the domain (DNS); health checks monitor the ALB endpoint
2 The Route 53 Alias A record resolves the domain to the Application Load Balancer
3 Users send HTTPS requests: Internet Users → Internet Gateway → ALB
4 AWS WAF Web ACL (OWASP Top 10 rules) associated with the ALB inspects and filters requests
5 ALB HTTPS :443 listener → Target Group → healthy EC2 instances in private subnets (both AZs)
6 Application tier queries the RDS MySQL primary; standby is a synchronous Multi-AZ replica
7 Static assets: Users → CloudFront (its own distribution domain or separate DNS record)
8 Cache miss: CloudFront origin request → ALB (assumed origin, via IGW); dynamic traffic bypasses CloudFront
Assumptions: MySQL engine (brief allows MySQL or PostgreSQL); ALB is the assumed CloudFront origin.
